body: Update: In a test project, I have two scenes. One has a new AnimatedSprite2D, let's call it Sprite A, and the second scene has an old AnimatedSprite2D with the bug I described, let's call it Sprite B. I tested it on all versions of 4.5, and Sprite B remained buggy, but Sprite A remained normal and working. I returned to 4.4 and then updated again, with the same result: Sprite A remained normal and Sprite B was buggy as always. I believe this is a "normal" migration bug to a different version of the engine. The solution I found is super simple: click on the problematic node (right-hand corner) and go to "Change Node," then select the same node. The problem disappears, but it doesn't delete anything, so the animations still exist. The reason for the issue is that this only occurred in 4.5 beta 5 and other earlier versions, as far as I can tell, but when I create a new AnimatedSprite2D, the problem disappears.

I did some tests and i can confirm the issue in v4.3.dev4.official [df78c0636], v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee], v4.5.beta5.official [c81fd6c51] and latest master [0c51ede](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/0c51ede2434d99d2c80dc87b7df179db66537f1c). The problem doesn't come from the `AnimatedSprite2D` per se, but from the `AnimationTree` node. For some reason the `AnimationNodeStateMachine` inside the `AnimationTree` node keeps calling the RESET track of the `AnimationPlayer` and that revert any attempt of change the current animation from the `AnimatedSprite2D`.
Checking with a debbuger is possible to notice how the editor continuosly call `AnimatedSprite2D::set_animation` to "idle" (the value stored in the RESET track). If no RESET track was created, the editor will try to set the animation to an empty string instead:
Video 1 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f608a5f7-3fc9-42c3-88e8-8b11efa283fd


Selecting the `AnimationTree` node and after the `AnimationPlayer` node temporarily solves the issue until you select the `AnimationTree` node again or close the scene.
Video 2 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e792fd02-63c8-468e-9c97-7811112660dc


And changing the property `Discrete` from the `AnimationTree` to `Dominant` or `Recessive` permanently fixes the issue:
Video 3 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efd41589-3316-4161-9d44-cb82b214c797


Also reverting pr #86629 fixes the issue, so pinging @TokageItLab to judge if this is a expected behavior or a bug.

Duplicate of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/110339. This is intentional.

> And changing the property Discrete from the AnimationTree to Dominant or Recessive permanently fixes the issue:

Also you can deactivate the AnimationTree to make it editable.
